stories.title: A creator-led Minecraft tournament drew more than 28 million viewing hours on Kick
paragraphs: Streams Charts says Dedsafio 4, a Spanish-language survival competition organized by streamer ElDed, generated 28.79 million hours watched on Kick in its first 14 days across 312 participating channels.

Its cross-stream peak reached about 1.07 million viewers in synchronized five-minute scans. Minecraft viewing on Kick rose from 2.9 million hours in the preceding two weeks to 30.33 million during the event's first half.

The report says the event was set to run through October 17. It illustrates the scale a coordinated creator event can bring to a game and platform, though the audience totals come from Streams Charts rather than platform-published figures.

scoreNotes.general: A large Spanish-language creator event shows how collaborative game formats can move audiences and game categories on a livestream platform.
scoreNotes.heat: Streams Charts reports 28.79 million viewing hours across 312 channels in the first 14 days, with a combined concurrent peak above one million. The figures are from one analytics outlet.
scoreNotes.time: The October 7 report covers September 21 to October 4; the event was scheduled to continue through October 17, so its first-half data is current seven-day context rather than a new 24-hour development.
scoreNotes.ethos: Streams Charts provides detailed platform estimates and identifies the event window. The report's underlying measurement method was not independently checked in this pass.

stories.title: Ubisoft sets a January shutdown for Rainbow Six Mobile
paragraphs: Ubisoft says Rainbow Six Mobile will remain available until January 15, 2027, after which the tactical shooter will close. The announcement sets an end date for a mobile live service built around the Rainbow Six franchise.

In one sampled Rainbow Six Reddit discussion, some commenters expressed surprise while others said the closure was expected. That thread is a limited snapshot, and the checked announcement did not provide player counts or a reason for the decision.

scoreNotes.general: A planned service closure affects players of a recognizable tactical-shooter franchise and offers a clear live-service outcome to track.
scoreNotes.heat: Ending a live mobile game is consequential for its players, although this search did not find a public player or revenue figure explaining the decision.
scoreNotes.time: The shutdown announcement appeared within the seven-day fallback window; Ubisoft says service will remain available until January 15, 2027.
scoreNotes.ethos: Ubisoft's developer message confirms the service end date. A sampled Reddit thread shows mixed reactions but cannot represent the whole player base.

stories.title: Militsioner opens its complete first act as a free Steam demo
paragraphs: Developer Tallboys and publisher Critical Reflex made a free Militsioner demo public on Steam on October 9. The stealth adventure centers on escaping a town watched by a giant policeman and its residents.

The demo contains the first act from beginning to end. 4Gamer says the team revised the town, characters, exploration, and guidance after earlier testing, including expanding a mind-map feature in response to feedback that players could lose track of their goals.
The public trial gives players a substantial look at the game's unusual mechanics, but the checked sources provide no player-count or reception data yet.

scoreNotes.general: A distinctive indie project has moved from anticipation to a substantial public trial that lets players experience its core design.
scoreNotes.heat: The public demo includes the full first act and mechanics built around stealth, social choices, and a giant policeman, but the checked reporting offers no audience-size measure.
scoreNotes.time: 4Gamer reported the demo launch on October 9, inside the seven-day fallback window.
scoreNotes.ethos: 4Gamer's dated report describes the public Steam demo and its contents. Player reception and demand remain unmeasured here.
